(a) Find ∫(6x+7)dx. [3]

(b) Given f′(x)=6x+7 and f(1.2)=7.32, find f(x). [3]
records.independentSolutionText: (a) ∫(6x+7)dx=3x²+7x+C. (b) f(x)=3x²+7x+C. Substituting x=1.2 gives 7.32=3(1.2)²+7(1.2)+C=12.72+C, so C=−5.4. Therefore f(x)=3x²+7x−5.4.

The coordinate graph shows the unshaded quadrilateral region R with vertices (1, 1), (5, 5), (6, 5), and (6, 1). The boundaries y = x and x = 6 are dashed, while y = 1 and y = 5 are solid. Find the inequalities that define the unshaded region R.
records.independentSolutionText: The region is below the dashed line y = x, so y < x. It lies to the left of the dashed line x = 6, so x < 6. The solid horizontal boundaries are included: y ≥ 1 and y ≤ 5. Therefore the inequalities are y < x, x < 6, 1 ≤ y ≤ 5.
